native_result.query: In which domain did both original and replication studies primarily use student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%)?
native_result.HypoA: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
native_result.HypoB: Social (social psychology) is the domain in which both original and replication studies predominantly used student subjects: in the Social discipline about 82-85% of original studies and 78-82% of replications used student samples, the closest alignment with the quoted 82.4% (original) and 80.9% (replication). Cognitive originals used students less often (~71-76%), and Economics, though nearly all student-based (~94-100%), has only 18 pairs and does not match the quoted percentages. Note: the exact quoted figures could not be reproduced exactly from the CSV under any simple cut and are treated as approximate source-publication values; domain selection is based on closest alignment.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Loaded the study-level CSV (927 rows, 141 unique O/R pair ids; projects ml1/ml3/rpp/ee) and quantified missingness (subjects.o 1, subjects.r 1, discipline 0, project 0). 2) Deduplicated to one row per pair id, preferring the aggregated==True row (26 ids) else the first row; verified subjects.o is constant within every id and discipline is constant within every id. 3) Computed the share of subjects=='students' per discipline (Social, Cognitive, Economics) for subjects.o and subjects.r at the pair level (main) and at the row/lab level (sensitivity), counting 'anyone', 'community', 'online' and NaN as non-students. 4) Sensitivity checks: excluded the 10 pair ids entirely flagged drop==True; examined the 16 ml1 ids whose subjects.r varies across labs (aggregated rows all record 'students'); handled the single missing-subjects row rpp.154 by excluding it from denominators. 5) Computed a joint measure (both original and replication used students) and the distance of each discipline's shares to the quoted 82.4%/80.9%; Social is closest at both levels, so the answer is Social. 6) The second CSV (143 rows) has no subjects/discipline columns and was used only to verify project naming. Supporting outputs: outputs/analysis_output.txt (console log), outputs/students_by_discipline_pair_level.csv, outputs/students_by_discipline_row_level.csv.

sub_hypo.text: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).
sub_hypo.context: Original and replication studies in Psychology.
sub_hypo.relations: Students predominated in both original studies (82.4%) and replications (80.9%). Community members accounted for 7.4% of original studies and 8.8% of replications; anyone accounted for 10.3% and 5.9%, respectively. Online participants accounted for 4.4% of replications.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: In Psychology, both original and replication studies primarily used student subjects (original: 82.4%, replication: 80.9%), but some also included community members (original: 7.4%, replication: 8.8%), anyone (original: 10.3%, replication: 5.9%), or online participants (replication: 4.4%).

sub_hypo.text: Social psychology is the domain whose original and replication student-sample shares most closely align with the approximate source-publication figures of 82.4% and 80.9%, respectively.
sub_hypo.context: Original–replication studies from projects ml1, ml3, rpp, and ee: 927 rows representing 141 pairs. Main analysis uses one row per pair, preferring aggregated rows; sensitivity analyses use row/lab-level data, exclude pairs entirely flagged for dropping, and exclude the single missing-subjects row from denominators.
sub_hypo.relations: Social originals used students in approximately 82–85% of studies and Social replications in approximately 78–82%. These shares are closest to the quoted 82.4%/80.9% at both pair and row/lab levels. Student use is defined as subjects=='students'; other categories and, in the main analysis, missing values count as non-students. Exact quoted percentages were not reproduced and are treated as approximate.

sub_hypo.text: Cognitive original studies used student samples less often than Social original studies.
sub_hypo.context: Original studies in the Cognitive and Social disciplines within the analyzed original–replication dataset, assessed using pair-level analysis and sensitivity checks.
sub_hypo.relations: Approximately 71–76% of Cognitive originals used students, compared with approximately 82–85% of Social originals.

sub_hypo.text: Economics studies were nearly all student-based but did not match the quoted original and replication student-sample percentages.
sub_hypo.context: The Economics discipline in the analyzed original–replication dataset, comprising only 18 pairs.
sub_hypo.relations: Economics student-sample shares were approximately 94–100%, exceeding rather than closely matching the quoted 82.4% for originals and 80.9% for replications.

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Social (social psychology) is the domain in which both original and replication studies predominantly used student subjects: in the Social discipline about 82-85% of original studies and 78-82% of replications used student samples, the closest alignment with the quoted 82.4% (original) and 80.9% (replication). Cognitive originals used students less often (~71-76%), and Economics, though nearly all student-based (~94-100%), has only 18 pairs and does not match the quoted percentages. Note: the exact quoted figures could not be reproduced exactly from the CSV under any simple cut and are treated as approximate source-publication values; domain selection is based on closest alignment.
